blocks.h2: Reasons to Get a Sewer Camera Inspection in McHenry
blocks.intro: The most common reasons we're called out:

tiles.body: Know what the sewer line looks like before closing, not after the first backup.

tiles.h3: The Same Clog Keeps Coming Back
tiles.body: A camera shows whether it's a sag, roots or a break.
If the Fox River or the lakes have been high, check whether groundwater is getting into a cracked line.
Confirm the line and floor drains are sound before new finishes go in.

blocks.h2: What We Find in McHenry Sewer Lines
blocks.intro: Most McHenry homes were built between 1970 and 2009. Here's what their lines tend to show.

items.body: Standing water in a section of pipe means it has settled. We measure where it starts, where it ends and how deep it is.
Common in 1970s and 1980s homes with mature trees.
Near the river and lakes, cracked joints can let groundwater into the line.
Sometimes the pipe is fine and just needs cleaning. That's good news.
Outside city sewer, we camera the line from the house to the septic tank to separate a pipe problem from a tank problem.

blocks.h2: How a Camera Inspection Works With Us
blocks.intro: You see exactly what we see.

steps.body: We mark the spot and depth of every problem.
What matters, what doesn't, and a copy of the video.

blocks.h2: Sewer Camera Questions From McHenry Homeowners

items.q: Should I get a sewer inspection before buying in McHenry?
items.preview: Yes. A home inspection doesn't look inside the sewer.
items.answer: Yes. A standard home inspection doesn't include the sewer line. A camera inspection can reveal a sag or break that's worth negotiating before you close.

items.q: Can a camera find a sag?
items.preview: Yes. Standing water in the pipe shows exactly where it is.
items.answer: Yes. A sag shows up as water sitting in the pipe. We measure its length and depth so a repair can target it.

items.q: Can you inspect a line to a septic tank?
items.answer: Yes. We can camera the line from the house to the tank and tell you if the problem is the pipe or the tank.

items.q: Do I get a copy of the video?
How long does an inspection take?
items.preview: About an hour for most homes.
items.answer: About an hour for most homes, including walking you through the video.

items.q: How much does a sewer camera inspection cost in McHenry?
items.preview: It depends on access and line length. You get a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on access and the length of the line. We give you a flat-rate price before any work begins.
